messages:
maria: FYI -- got a burst of pagers for embed-serving around 21:05 UTC, looks like KV cache thrash + a couple of OOM restarts. I'm handing primary to @aj for the evening. leaving quick pointers below.

oncall-bot: Pager opened INC-4321 at 2026-03-14T21:05:12Z -> severity: P1, affected: embeddings service, region: us-west2. Active responders: maria, aj, sam-prod.

aj: taking primary. thanks @maria. quick question — any ongoing customer-facing errors or just internal retries?

sam-prod: customer-facing 5xxs for streaming embeddings from a couple of high-volume tenants. Rate of failing requests peaked at ~12% for a 10m window then trended down to ~3%. I opened a monitoring alert (embed-errors > 1% for 5m).

lee-sre: root cause looks like KV shard pressure leading to eviction storms. runtime logs show repeated cache misses followed by cold-load spikes. Also saw a few host restarts -> tokenization worker OOMs.

maria: quick mitigation steps I did: 1) scaled embeddings pool by +2 replicas (short burst), 2) disabled aggressive batching on the high-traffic route, 3) forced KV grace period to 30s. Not ideal long term but bought time.

carla: thanks. can you paste the exact scale command you used? want to run in eu if needed.

maria: sure — ran:
```
kubectl -n redwood scale deploy embed-ingesters --replicas=8
# then bump autoscaler min to 6 temporarily
kubectl patch hpa embed-ingesters -p '{"spec": {"minReplicas": 6}}'
```

aj: ok doing cross-region ramp in eu as precaution. Also toggling the runtime flag to reduce kv eviction aggressiveness:
```
# set via featureflags service
POST https://infra-api.redwood.internal/flags
{ "service": "embeddings", "FLAG_KV_EVICT_FACTOR": "0.6" }
```

oncall-bot: Note: changing flags will restart a subset of pods (can be staggered). Suggest canary 10% -> 30% -> 100%.

lee-sre: runbook refs: KV cache stall & eviction playbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-eviction-storm (follow section "quick rollback" if changes worsen latency). Also embedding service ops: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-runtime.

sam-prod: quick checklist for whoever's primary: 
- keep the temporary scale in place until error rate <1% for 15m
- if errors increase after flag change, rollback flag immediately and reduce concurrency on the ingesters
- alert owners on affected accounts (INC-4321) with customer-impact template

carla: created the incident ticket with affected tenants, added SRE and support pings. https://tracker.redwood/INC-4321

dave: one-off tip — if you see sustained OOMs on tokenizers, try lowering chunk_size to 1024 for the heavy tenants. cheap and usually reduces memory pressure.

aj: doing canary flag rollout now (10%). watching logs and APM traces. will advance after 5m stable.

maria: small note: we saw one side-effect where lowering eviction made token cache grow on restart. keep an eye on pod memory. If mem climbs >85% over 3m, rollback.

aj: canary looks OK for 10m, errors down to ~1.2%. advancing to 30%.

oncall-bot: Rollout update: 10% -> 30% at 2026-03-14T21:24:00Z by aj.

lee-sre: if 30% still stable, recommend increasing request timeout on the public embed endpoint to 20s temporarily to avoid client-side retries exacerbating load. config: https://config.redwood/internal/services/embeddings -> REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS

aj: 30% stable, pushing to 100%. monitoring error rates and latency.

sam-prod: notify Support to tell affected customers we mitigated an embed degradation — include ETA for full postmortem. Use template: "We observed increased errors for embeddings around 21:05 UTC; mitigation in progress; we will follow up with details and RCA."

maria: ok, @aj, you're primary for the rest of the night. leaving runbook shortlinks in the thread. if you escalate to infra, @lee-sre is the primary SRE on-call.

aj: got it. logging a quick handoff note in the oncall doc. things to follow up tomorrow: investigate shard sizing, consider prefix-aware caching, and add an automated alarm for KV eviction rate.

carla: also scheduled a brief post-incident sync for 11:00 UTC tomorrow with product and support.

dave: final ops tip — if you need a faster short-term fix, enable request-level caching for the top 5 tenants (edge cache) which drops backend load immediately. config snippet: https://redwood.internal/snippets/edge-cache-quickenable

aj: thanks everyone. closing the active pager for now while we watch. will re-open if anything regresses. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Pager INC-4321 marked "mitigated" at 2026-03-14T21:44:30Z by aj.

maria: nice work team. final handoff: @aj primary until 2026-03-15T07:00Z, @maria secondary. added runbook tags + ticket links to the oncall doc.

aj: night team, I'll post a short incident summary in #postmortems and add the telemetry graphs.

carla: thanks — closing notes: follow-up owners: lee-sre (shard sizing), sam-prod (alerts tuning), dave (edge cache template). I'll convert INC-4321 to a postmortem ticket tomorrow.
